issues.legal_issue: A tenant’s challenge to the validity of a limited tenancy must ordinarily be raised before the tenancy expires and cannot be raised as a defence to a later application for possession, except in a narrowly limited case where the tenant establishes that there was no earlier opportunity to learn the relevant facts and learned them only later.
material_facts: The landlord and tenant appeared before the Rent Controller, who approved a residential limited tenancy for a fixed two-year term after recording their statements.
The tenant remained in the premises after the term expired, and the landlord then applied for possession.
The tenant first objected to the validity of the limited tenancy in response to the post-expiry application for possession.
The tenant did not establish that he had no opportunity to learn the relevant facts before the tenancy expired or that he learned them only afterward.
issues.conclusion: The tenant’s belated objection should not have been entertained, and the landlord’s application for possession should have been granted.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 21 of the Delhi Rent Control Act, 1958, a challenge to the validity of a limited tenancy should be brought during the tenancy, when the tenant becomes aware, or with diligence could become aware, of facts supporting the challenge. The exception is confined to an exceptional case in which the tenant satisfies the Controller that there was no opportunity to know the facts earlier and that awareness arose only later. Section 21 provides a limited-tenancy procedure distinct from the ordinary protection against eviction under section 14. The Court confined S.B. Noronah v. Prem Kumari Khanna, [1980] 1 SCR 281, to its facts and relied on J.R. Vohra v. India Export House Pvt. Ltd., [1985] 2 SCR 899, Inder Mohan Lal v. Ramesh Khanna, [1987] 4 SCC 1, and Shiv Chander Kapoor v. Amar Bose, JT 1989 (4) SC 471; it treated suggestions in Vohra and Shiv Chander Kapoor that a post-expiry objection might be examined as obiter, subject to the narrow exception.

predicates.limited_tenancy_proceeding: The proceeding concerns a tenancy created for a fixed limited term under a special procedure that provides for possession at the end of the term.
predicates.tenant_challenged_validity_after_expiry: The tenant first challenged the validity of the limited tenancy after its term had expired, in response to an application for possession.
predicates.tenant_had_earlier_opportunity_to_learn_: The tenant had an opportunity to learn the facts supporting the challenge before the term expired, rather than establishing that those facts became knowable only afterward.

issues.definition: When a tenant in a limited-tenancy proceeding first challenges validity after expiry despite an earlier opportunity to learn the relevant facts, the objection is not entertained at that late stage.
